text:
$BTC hovered at $85,790, down 0.82% in 24 h. It peaked near $86,999 before slipping to a low of $84,972, the widest swing of the three. Quote volume topped $1.38 B, the heaviest flow across the set.

$ETH slipped 0.50% to $2,712.11. The pair traded between $2,738 and $2,680, a tighter band than BTC. Volume hit about 269 K ETH, translating to $730 M in USDT.

$BNB took the biggest hit, down 1.10% to $786.09. Its range was narrow, $809.99 high, $784.70 low, but the 142 K BNB traded moved $113 M in quote volume, the second-largest dollar amount.

All three ended the day lower, with BTC leading on range, BNB on percent drop, and BTC still carrying the bulk of dollar volume.

$TSLAB is hanging at 375.28 USDT, up 0.722% after peaking 379.1 USDT and testing a low of 365.27 USDT. Volume's sitting around 2.64 M USDT, so the token's still moving while the traditional market sleeps.

Cerebras' bStock ($CBRSB) nudged higher, closing at 184.17 USDT with a 1.87% gain. It bounced off a 173.3 USDT low, touched 186.15 USDT, and pushed 2.42 M USDT of volume through the night.

Micron ($MUB) barely shifted, down 0.103% to 1,067.62 USDT. The range was tight, high 1,081.19 USDT, low 1,056.45 USDT, and volume hovered near 2.56 M USDT. All three bStocks kept the 24/7 grind going.

$ADA ripped up 10.66% in the last 24 hours, which is about 1.6 times its usual daily swing. That's noticeably wider than its week-average range, and the price now sits around $0.2692. Nothing else to flag right now.

$STRK surged 14.7% to $0.0593, trading near its high of $0.0596 with 23.4 M USDT volume. Meanwhile $QNT slipped 5.4% down to $251.5, still under its recent high of $278.3 and moving about 51.7 M USDT. $FET also jumped, up 11.6% to $0.2521, hugging the top of its range at $0.2599 on 35.8 M USDT. The market's pulling a few small caps ahead while the heavyweight $QNT drags behind. Nothing wild, just a split-personality session.

$BTC closed at $85,284, up about 0.5% after bouncing between $84,558 and $85,428. It nudged higher on the upside, capped the day near the high, then steadied back into the mid-$85K range.

$ETH ended around $2,703, gaining roughly 0.7% while trading in a tight band from $2,677 to $2,708. The price slipped a bit early, recovered, and finished just above the day's peak.

$BNB was the standout, jumping 2.25% to $788.49. It swung from a low of $770.47 up to $795.12, carving out the widest range of the three and hauling the most quote volume at about $84.3 M.

Overall, a modest rally for BTC and ETH, but BNB's burst gave the market its only real spark.

$ETH is up 0.316% against $BTC, so it's pulling a hair ahead of Bitcoin. $BTC itself rose 0.307% in the last 24 h. Meanwhile the median alt in the 19-coin basket jumped 2.252%, outpacing both majors nicely. In short, Bitcoin's still ticking up, but the broader alt set is doing the heavy lifting, and ETH is gaining a touch of relative strength versus $BTC. Nothing wild, just a modest spread between the leaders.

$CBRSB just ripped up 6.75% to 178.61 USDT, swinging between a low of 167.09 and a high of 178.63. Volume's over a million USDT, so the tokenized stock stayed busy while traditional markets were closed.

$NVDAB barely budged, up 0.46% at 235.06 USDT. It hovered right around its high of 235.07 and low of 233.87, with roughly 845k USDT changing hands.

$SPYB crept up 0.14% to 770.84 USDT, trading in a tight 769.12-771.14 band and pulling about 108k USDT in volume. All three keep moving 24/7, so you can catch these moves any hour.

$SAND jumped about twice its usual daily swing, ripping a 32% range while its typical spread sits near 12%. The token closed the day up 20% at $0.07645. That's a lot more movement than we normally see. Nothing else crazy on the board.

$SAND jumped 28% to $0.0765, blasting past its $0.057 low and flashing a $85 M quote volume. $QNT also pushed up, up 16% to $268.96, holding near the top of its $224-$270 range with $73 M traded. Meanwhile $PUMP slipped 9% to $0.0055, hovering close to its $0.0051 trough after a brief peek at $0.0062 and pulling in $47 M. The winners are sprinting ahead while the loser is barely hanging on. Looks like a typical day of a few rockets and one deflator.
